beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: AI can produce an answer, but who takes responsibility for the work?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That gap is the reason to open AssistOS.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This book explores a workplace where people delegate to persistent software workers.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its central concern is what happens around intelligence: responsibility, continuity, and control.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You will encounter a different way to think about using AI.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The question shifts from choosing a model to organizing work you can trust.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book develops that shift through ordinary assignments and their hidden complications.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This introduction offers a taste of those ideas and a route into the book.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A good conversation can end while the practical work remains scattered.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Files live elsewhere, decisions lose their context, and the next task starts again.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: AssistOS examines what is missing between a capable agent and a dependable working relationship.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It proposes giving virtual workers roles, projects, histories, and bounded authority.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book brings those concerns together as an operating layer around AI capabilities.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That is the perspective its technical details are meant to serve.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: For the reader, it opens a useful question about every promising AI demonstration.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: What would have to surround this capability before someone could depend on it?
